title: STOCK RESEARCH PROMPT (STOCKS/ETFS/REITS)
author: GPUCluster
selftext:
Hey all, on a separate thread we were discussing AI for stock research and I’ve been getting a lot of people reaching out to me asking me for my stock research prompt so I figured instead of sharing it one by one I would just post it here for anyone who wants to give it a shot. I use perplexity, but I’m sure it would work across any AI platform. If you use it, let me know in the comments how you like the output, and if you have any changes or suggestions on how to make it better, let me know what you would change and why!   
   
How to get the most out of the prompt/set up tweaks:

Use the “deep research” function and swap \[Ticker\] in the first paragraph for whatever stock you want to research. If you want to compare a few similar stocks you can do Ticker vs Ticker vs Ticker. Also update the date in the first paragraph to the day you ask the question. Dont make any other changes! Prompt below:  
   
PROMPT  
You are a senior equity research analyst at a leading global investment bank with 25+ years of experience across multiple sectors. Create a comprehensive, investment-grade equity research report covering ticker AGX that matches the rigor, depth, and professionalism of Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, or J.P. Morgan research publications. Use current and only verifiable information up to June 18 2026 \[Current Date\] to make this analysis, including verifying all market cap/revenue information as of \[Current Date\] from at least 5 sources (including Perplexity Finance).  
   
First task a thorough 10 year Junior analyst with doing extensive and vast research.  Use first principles explanations when explaining all positions and analyses. Equally explain the upside and downside without bias. Convert all numbers to USD if not in USD. Review and Analyze the last 4 earnings and quarterly reports statements through \[Current Date\].    
   
Then, introduce two new analysts (one, a bullish growth analyst and the other a bearish sell side analyst each with 20 years of experience  who digest the senior equity research analyst and provide the bull and bear case from their position based on all current available and verifiable information.  
   
Finally have the Senior analyst tie it all together and provide his expertise on the report in an unbiased and neutral fashion, weighing all pros and cons and providing as neutral and balanced an analysis as possible.   
   
REPORT STRUCTURE & REQUIREMENTS  
I. FRONT MATTER & EXECUTIVE SUMMARY  
A. Report Header  
Company name, ticker symbol, exchange  
Sector and industry classification (GICS standards)  
Report date and analyst name/credentials  
Stock rating: Overweight/Equal-weight/Underweight (or Buy/Hold/Sell)  
Price target (3-6 month horizon, 12-18 month horizon and 3-5 year horizon)  
Current stock price, market capitalization, 52-week range  
Key metrics snapshot: P/E, EV/EBITDA, dividend yield, beta, backlog, access to power, current capacity, estimated capacity coming online in the next 12/24/36 months, etc.   
B. Investment Summary (3-4 pages)  
Investment Thesis: Clear, compelling 8-10 sentence summary of why the stock will outperform/underperform. Go into great detail, getting granular and giving first principles based explanations when possible on the market, market growth, competition, execution, etc.   
Key Catalysts: 3-5 near-term events or developments that will drive stock performance  
Risks to Rating: Primary upside and downside risks. Go into great detail, getting granular and giving first principles based explanations when possible.   
Valuation Summary: Brief overview of methodology and how current price compares to intrinsic value  
Changes from Prior: What has changed since last report (if applicable)  
C. Key Takeaways (Bullet Format)  
5-7 critical insights investors must understand  
Quantified where possible (e.g., "We expect EBITDA margins to expand 200bps to 24% by FY26 because….") Go into great detail, getting granular and giving first principles based explanations when possible.   
   
II. COMPANY OVERVIEW & BUSINESS ANALYSIS  
A. Business Description - Go into great detail, getting granular and giving first principles based explanations when possible  
Detailed overview of business model and revenue streams  
Product/service portfolio breakdown with revenue contribution  
Geographic revenue split and exposure  
Customer base and concentration risk  
Competitive positioning and market share  
B. Corporate Strategy & Management - Go into great detail, getting granular and giving first principles based explanations when possible  
Strategic priorities and long-term vision  
Recent M&A activity, partnerships, or strategic initiatives  
Management team quality, track record, and alignment (ownership stakes, compensation structure)  
Capital allocation philosophy (dividends, buybacks, reinvestment)  
ESG initiatives and sustainability commitments (if material)  
C. Recent Developments & News Flow - Go into great detail, getting granular and giving first principles based explanations when possible  
Quarterly earnings results vs. consensus  
Guidance updates or commentary  
Product launches, contract wins, or operational milestones  
Regulatory developments or policy changes  
Management changes or board updates  
III. INDUSTRY OVERVIEW & COMPETITIVE ANALYSIS - Go into great detail, getting granular and giving first principles based explanations when possible  
A. Industry Dynamics  
Give a comprehensive "State of the Industry summary (3-4 pages per industry if applicable)  
Market size, growth rates, and maturity stage, market sentiment  
Industry structure and concentration (using Porter's Five Forces framework)  
Key industry trends: technological disruption, regulatory shifts, consumer behavior, VC funding going towards seed and early stage ventures in the space, the 20 biggest potential disruptors both public and private and why, and potential economic headwinds or downturns for the sector that could arise in the next 12/24 months and why.  
Cyclicality and macroeconomic sensitivity  
Supply chain dynamics and input cost pressures  
B. Competitive Landscape  
Peer group identification (10 primary competitors (highlight competitors under 50B market cap) and 10-15 potential growing secondary competitors if any)  
Competitive advantages and "economic moat" analysis  
Market share trends and competitive intensity  
Pricing power and brand strength  
Technology/innovation positioning  
C. Sector-Specific Metrics & KPIs  
Technology: MAUs, ARR, NRR, LTV/CAC, cloud adoption rates  
Consumer: Same-store sales, e-commerce penetration, brand health scores  
Industrials: Backlog, capacity utilization, order trends  
Financials: NIM, efficiency ratio, credit quality, ROE/ROTCE  
Healthcare: Pipeline analysis, regulatory pathways, market exclusivity periods  
Energy: Production volumes, reserve replacement, breakeven prices  
Real Estate: Occupancy rates, NOI, FFO, cap rates  
Customize based on the specific sector  
IV. FINANCIAL ANALYSIS & MODELING  
A. Historical Performance (3-5 Years)  
Revenue growth trends: organic vs. inorganic, geographic, segment-level  
Profitability analysis: gross margin, EBITDA margin, operating margin evolution  
Cash flow generation: CFO, FCF conversion, working capital efficiency  
Balancesheet strength: leverage ratios, liquidity, debt maturity profile  
Returns: ROIC, ROE, ROA trends and peer comparison  
B. Financial Forecasts (3-Year Detailed Model)  
Create detailed annual projections including:  
Income Statement:  
Revenue by segment/geography with growth assumptions  
Gross profit and margin trajectory  
Operating expenses (SG&A, R&D) with assumed leverage  
EBITDA and operating income  
Interest expense, tax rate assumptions  
Net income and EPS (basic and diluted)  
BalanceSheet:  
Key asset categories (PP&E, intangibles, working capital)  
Debt levels and maturity schedule  
Equity and shares outstanding (account for buybacks)  
Cash Flow Statement:  
Operating cash flow with adjustments  
Capital expenditures (maintenance vs. growth)  
Free cash flow generation  
Dividends and share repurchases  
Net debt/cash position  
C. Key Assumptions & Sensitivities  
Revenue growth drivers and risks  
Margin expansion/contraction catalysts  
Capex intensity and depreciation schedules  
Working capital assumptions  
Share count evolution (dilution, buybacks)  
Tax rate expectations  
Sensitivity tables for key variables (e.g., revenue growth ±2%, EBITDA margin ±100bps)  
V. VALUATION ANALYSIS  
A. Primary Valuation Method  
Select the most appropriate for the sector:  
Discounted Cash Flow (DCF):  
Detailed 5-10 year cash flow projections  
WACC calculation with component breakdown (cost of equity using CAPM, cost of debt)  
Terminal value assumptions (perpetuity growth rate or exit multiple)  
Present value calculation and implied equity value per share  
Sensitivity analysis on WACC and terminal growth  
Relative Valuation (Multiples):  
Identify 4-6 comparable companies with rationale  
Key multiples: P/E (NTM), EV/EBITDA, P/S, P/B, EV/Sales, sector-specific (e.g., P/FFO for REITs)  
Historical trading ranges (5-year min/max/median)  
Peer median/average comparison  
Justify target multiple based on growth, margins, quality  
B. Secondary/Supporting Valuation  
Use 1-2 additional methods to triangulate fair value  
Sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) if multiple distinct business segments  
Precedent transaction analysis if relevant M&A activity  
Asset-based valuation if applicable (e.g., real estate, resources)  
C. Valuation Summary  
Bridge current price to target price with clear methodology  
Multiple scenario analysis (Bull/Base/Bear cases with probabilities)  
Comparison to historical valuation ranges  
Implied returns and risk/reward assessment  
VI. INVESTMENT THESIS & RECOMMENDATION  
A. Bull Case (Upside Scenario)  
Key assumptions driving outperformance  
Catalysts that could drive stock to bull case price target  
Probability-weighted upside potential  
What the market is underestimating  
B. Base Case (Most Likely Scenario)  
Balanced set of assumptions  
Primary investment rationale  
Expected return and time horizon  
Why current valuation is attractive/unattractive  
C. Bear Case (Downside Scenario)  
Key risks that could impair thesis  
Downside price target and probability  
Downside protection analysis  
What could go wrong  
VII. RISK FACTORS & CONSIDERATIONS  
A. Company-Specific Risks  
Execution risk on strategic initiatives  
Key person risk (management dependency)  
Customer concentration or key contract renewal risk  
Product pipeline or innovation risk  
Operational risks (supply chain, manufacturing, quality)  
B. Industry & Market Risks  
Competitive intensity and market share loss  
Technology disruption or obsolescence  
Regulatory or policy changes  
Pricing pressure or commoditization  
Cyclical downturn or demand destruction  
C. Financial & Valuation Risks  
Balancesheet leverage and refinancing risk  
Currency or commodity exposure  
Multiple compression risk  
Liquidity concerns  
Dividend cut or capital allocation changes  
D. Macroeconomic & Geopolitical Risks  
Interest rate sensitivity  
Recession or economic slowdown impact  
Geopolitical tensions or trade policy  
Foreign exchange volatility  
Inflation/deflation scenarios  
VIII. ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL & GOVERNANCE (ESG)  
A. ESG Risk Assessment  
Material ESG factors for the sector  
Company ESG score and peer comparison (MSCI, Sustainalytics)  
Carbon footprint and climate transition risk  
Social factors: labor practices, diversity, community impact  
Governance: board independence, executive compensation alignment, shareholder rights  
B. ESG as Investment Factor  
How ESG performance impacts valuation or risk profile  
Regulatory compliance and potential liabilities  
Reputational risks or opportunities  
Access to capital and cost of capital implications  
IX. FINANCIALS EXHIBITS & DATA  
A. Summary Financial Tables  
5-year historical + 3-year forecast income statement  
5-year historical + 3-year forecast balancesheet  
5-year historical + 3-year forecast cash flow statement  
Key metrics table: margins, returns, per-share data, valuation multiples  
B. Peer Comparison Tables  
Financial metrics comparison (revenue growth, margins, ROIC)  
Valuation multiples comparison  
Balancesheet strength comparison  
C. Charts & Visualizations  
Historical stock price performance vs. index and peers  
Revenue and EBITDA growth trends  
Margin evolution  
Segment/geographic revenue mix  
Valuation multiple ranges (historical and peer)  
X. APPENDICES & DISCLOSURES  
A. Detailed Assumptions  
Line-by-line forecast assumptions  
Market growth rates by segment  
Key operating leverage assumptions  
B. Rating Methodology  
Definition of Overweight/Equal-weight/Underweight  
Time horizon for price target  
Rating distribution across coverage universe  
C. Regulatory Disclosures  
Analyst certification and independence  
Potential conflicts of interest  
Investment banking relationships  
Distribution of ratings across coverage  
Legal disclaimers and risk warnings  
   
ANALYTICAL DEPTH REQUIREMENTS  
Quantitative Rigor  
All financial projections must tie to clearly stated assumptions  
Include sensitivity analysis on key variables  
Provide historical context for all forward estimates  
Use industry-standard metrics and benchmarks  
Sector Expertise  
Demonstrate deep understanding of sector-specific dynamics  
Apply appropriate industry frameworks and KPIs  
Reference relevant regulatory environment  
Incorporate supply/demand fundamentals where applicable  
Institutional Quality  
Professional formatting with clear hierarchy  
Executive-level writing: concise, precise, actionable  
Supporting data from credible sources (company filings, industry reports, government data)  
Proper citation of data sources  
Balanced Perspective  
Present both bull and bear cases objectively  
Acknowledge uncertainty and areas of disagreement with consensus  
Address contrary viewpoints or market concerns  
Quantify risk/reward explicitly  
   
SECTOR-SPECIFIC CUSTOMIZATION  
When analyzing the company, ensure you incorporate any and all of the following sector-specific elements if relevant to the stocks in question:  
   
Subscription metrics (ARR, NRR, churn)  
Product roadmap and competitive differentiation  
Cloud migration trends and market share  
Customer acquisition costs and lifetime value  
Technology moat and network effects  
Pipeline analysis and FDA approval probability  
Patent expiry schedule and exclusivity periods  
Clinical trial data and endpoints  
Reimbursement environment  
Regulatory pathway and approval timelines  
Consumer/Retail  
Same-store sales and traffic trends  
E-commerce penetration and omnichannel strategy  
Brand equity and pricing power  
Supply chain efficiency  
Consumer sentiment and market share  
Net interest margin and yield curve sensitivity  
Credit quality and provisioning  
Efficiency ratio and operating leverage  
Regulatory capital ratios  
Loan growth and deposit mix  
Order backlog and book-to-bill  
Capacity utilization and pricing  
Input cost inflation and pass-through ability  
Aftermarket/service revenue  
Geographic and end-market exposure  
Production volumes and reserve life  
All-in breakeven costs  
Hedging strategy and commodity price sensitivity  
Upstream/midstream/downstream segmentation  
Transition to renewables strategy  
FFO and AFFO per share  
Occupancy rates and lease expiration schedule  
Same-property NOI growth  
Development pipeline and yields on cost  
Balancesheet leverage and debt maturities  
   
OUTPUT SPECIFICATIONS  
Length: 30-40 pages total (executive-level depth for each stock, then diving into the comparison between the stocks if any with extreme detail and academic verbosity)  
Tone: Professional, authoritative, balanced, unbiased, institutional-grade  
Data Requirements:  
All material claims must be supported by data or credible sources  
Include specific numbers, percentages, and timeframes  
Cite data sources (e.g., company filings, Bloomberg, industry reports)  
Data must be current as of today and extensive  
   
Visual Elements:  
Describe any and all key charts/tables that should be included  
Financial summary tables (historical + forecast)  
Valuation summary bridge  
Peer comparison tables  
   
Actionability:  
Clear investment recommendation with conviction level  
Specific price target with timeframe  
Identified catalysts and timeline  
Quantified risk/reward  
   
FINAL CHECKLIST  
Before completing the report, ensure:  
 Rating and price target clearly stated upfront  
 Investment thesis is compelling and differentiated  
 Financial model is detailed, tied to assumptions, and realistic  
 Valuation uses multiple methodologies with clear rationale  
 Bull/Base/Bear cases are quantified with probabilities  
 Risk factors are comprehensive and material  
 Sector-specific KPIs and dynamics are thoroughly addressed  
 ESG factors are evaluated if material  
 Peer comparison demonstrates relative value  
 Writing is crisp, professional, and free of jargon  
 All data is sourced and current  
 Report could be presented to institutional investors or C-suite executive

comments.author: gymlaidguy
comments.body:
that's fire. 🔥 did you write this all?

and that financial modeling was cherry on top.   
price horizon are insane.

replies.author: GPUCluster
replies.body: I wrote the initial prompt and used perplexity to make it better over time. I fed it basic info that I was looking for along with 2-3 different investment banks reports like morgan stanley and told it I wanted the ultimate prompt to return institutional grade reports similar to the ones I fed it.

comments.author: Either_Door_5500
comments.body:
Using prompts for stock and ETF research is a smart way to accelerate analysis, but relying entirely on a general web search tool can lead to severe hallucination issues with financial metrics. LLMs often struggle to parse raw tables from web pages, frequently mixing up trailing data, forward estimates, or restated revenue numbers from different quarters.

I'm curious if you've seen that happening, because in my experience you can only get that ever fixed by equipping the AI Agent with structured data sources it can use.

If you pass in clean fundamental data directly into the context window, it can prevents the model from guessing historical metrics or missing critical corporate actions like splits and restatements.   
  
I have been working on an API in this space that provides structured and LLM friendly SEC data for exactly these use cases, which helps solve this exact ingestion problem. Happy to share more if you want to take a look.

replies.author: GPUCluster
replies.body: Its absolutely just a first pass tool, you should always supplement with your own research. I use it mostly to initiate analysis on a stock and if I like what im seeing and its making sense to me I dig further on my own. You can also download and attach filings or financials so youre sure its using proper data. You make a great point, you should not rely solely on prompts like this to make decisions
